questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: GO HIKE. There is so many good hikes around Wellington and the whole of New Zealand. I were on two road trips around New Zealand. One in the mid semester break and another after the semester had ended - which I can highly recommend. Do a courise at Milford Sound, especially, if it is raining - 100's of waterfalls will spontanously be created. Otherwise just find different travel blogs and pick locations that look cool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since everyone speaks english. The vibe is very hipster and progressive in Wellington, so much like Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just say hi.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dunno. Go to the national museum Te Papa at the waterfront to learn about maori culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most of it. Kiwis low their nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for it be expenssive. Go see the country and so much nature, which cannot be found in Denmark. Do not stress about school. You only need 50% in a course to pass.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to apply for acocmendation in the given deadlines, to be sure to have housing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going on trips with my friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing school with social life. Wellington is very windy - get some proper cloth and you will quickly get used to it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go for it! :)
